newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan rebels capture provincial capital - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels capture provincial capital - paper.

text.p: A Sudan government-owned newspaper said on Tuesday that the provincial capital of Rumbek in the south of the country recently fell to rebels.

Al-Anbaa daily's report was the first time the Islamist government admitted the capture of the Buheyrat state capital, which Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) rebels said they took earlier this month.
The newspaper quoted an unnamed source as saying the rebels captured Rumbek on their third attempt with the help of local government officials. It did not say when.
"Saboteurs inside the town gave information from a minister at the government of Buheyrat to the rebels in which he revealed the points of weakness in the line of defence," it said.
The paper said the minister and one of the commissioners helped rebels arrest their colleagues when the city fell.
Rumbek is 380 km (235 miles) northwest of the southern capital of Juba, which rebel forces are slowly encircling. SPLA leader John Garang was reported this month as saying he was sure to seize Juba.

Forces under Garang's command have stepped up their war on three fronts this year through the Eritrea-based National Democratic Alliance (NDA) coalition with the aim of toppling Khartoum's government.
The Sudanese government has accused Eritrean, Ethiopian and Ugandan troops of taking part in rebel offensives in the south, east and northeast. The three countries denied the charges.
The SPLA has fought since 1983 for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north. The NDA says it aims to trigger an uprising in Khartoum.
